newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-KEEGAN WOULD RETURN TO BE ENGLAND COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEEGAN WOULD RETURN TO BE ENGLAND COACH.

text.p: Kevin Keegan, who quit as manager of Newcastle United in dramatic style in January, has hinted he may be interested in returning to soccer one day if he was offered the top job of England coach.
After resigning at Newcastle, the former England international midfielder said he was not planning a return to the game.
But in an interview in the British newspaper The People on Sunday, the 46-year-old Keegan said: "The only thing I would enjoy -- if it could happen -- would be to handle big name players for England.
"Anyone who played for England wonders about that job. Maybe managing England next...who knows?"

The former Liverpool, Hamburg and Southampton midfielder, who won 63 caps for his country, was linked with the job when England were looking for a replacement for Terry Venables after last year's European championship.
But, having signed a long-term deal with Newcastle, Keegan ruled himself out of the running and Glenn Hoddle was eventually appointed.
